newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 30.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The European Commission of the EU confirmed its negative opinion of the new import deposit system and called on the Czech cabinet to cancel this measure, because the Czech economy is not in bad enough shape to threaten trade.

- The governer of the Czech National Bank, who is meeting in Washington with the World Bank and the International Exchange Fund, said that he has not yet received any criticism of the central bank's exchange rate policy this year.
- Experts expect the crown to stay between two and three percent below parity for next few months.
- Daily production of Skoda Octavias is around 200, about half of Skoda's planned capacity for this year. More than 2,000 Octavias have been sold on the Czech market this year.
- During the five-day strike which is to begin today in Motol Hospital in Prague, all patients with acute conditions will still be examined.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Yesterday, police arrested two senior officials of Investicni a Postovni Banka. They are both accused of fraud and other economic crimes.
- Regional Development Minister Jaromir Schneider announced yesterday that he will resign from his position to the request of his party, the Christian Democrats.
- About 1,000 people gathered in front of the Health Ministry in Prague yesterday, protesting over the threatened fate of General Faculty Hospital.

- Fruit growers from all over the Czech Republic handed out apples to show people that they are just as good as those imported from the EU. They insist that the EU's current agreement with the Czech Republic for trade with apples is unfair to domestic growers.
- State-owned Konsolidacni Banka closed its accounts last year with losses of 5.1 billion crowns after aspiring to have profits of 737 million crowns.
- The new shareholders of the largest domestic crown funds proposed at a general meeting for the Czech National Investment Property Fund to reduce the basic capital of the funds by 10 percent.

PRAVO - German President Roman Herzog addressed Czech parliament yesterday, so ending the process of accepting the Czech-German Declaration. Herzog apologised to the Czechs and admitted historical responsibility for Munich in 1938 and the breaking and occupation of Czechoslovakia.
- The Industry and Trade Ministry finished a basic concept for a new trade law which should be accepted in the fall. It specifies conditions for foreigners setting up businesses.
- Skoda Klatovy, subsidiary of Skoda Plzen, and American Titan signed a contract to supply a complete factory for recycling tyres worth $10 million for Austrian clients.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The Slovak ambassador to the Czech Republic, Ivan Mjartan, who was called to Bratislava nearly three weeks ago due to worsening Czech-Slovak relations, returned to his Prague post yesterday.

- Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy announced the new list of imports which require an import deposit. The new list does not include 23 items from the old list, including certain paints and lacquers, photographic disks and film, rough-worked stones, certain paper products and heavy tractors.
- Real monthly wages increased month-on-month in March by 7.3 percent, according to the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU). Industrial businesses with 20 or more employees had less revenue last month.
- The commission for the tender for Aero Vodochody presented a proposal for the winner to the cabinet for approval. Experts expect CSA-Boeing to win the 34 percent stake.
